evidence: Turner’s first haridrā branch includes Prakrit haladdā/haliddā, Hindi haladdī/haldī, Gujarati haḷad/haḷdar and Marathi haḷad. The retained l/ḷ plus retroflex-stop survey forms and contracted Gujari hād fit that turmeric series; vowel and aspiration variation is preserved. The hāridra dyed-with-turmeric subsection is not selected.

The Noiri/Dungra elḍ- turmeric noun compares with Gujarati haḷad and Hindi haladdī in Turner’s haridrā branch. This placement allows initial h loss, contraction and the recorded initial e vowel; it is a regional lexical comparison, with the o/a endings retained and no claim to a newly established sound law.

Zoller explicitly derives Indus Kohistani həlīẓ/həlīṣ turmeric from haridrā (CDIAL 13992); Turner also gives Shina haliẓi. The survey hāliź/hæliṣ forms preserve this diagnostic northwestern outcome, including the source’s palatal/retroflex notation and final vowel where present. This is not the unrelated halīṣā plough-pole entry printed immediately above in Zoller.

Zoller explicitly compares Indus Kohistani huigi/hugi garlic to Pashto hūga. These closely matching survey forms are assigned as loans using the existing Pashto ūgā donor attestation; that node represents the Pashto lexical family, not a claim that the exact Charsadda vowel/initial realization was the local donor. Transmission through a neighbouring Kohistani variety remains possible.

Turner gives Gujarati kā̃dɔ, Marathi kā̃dā and Konkani kā̃ndo onion under kanda bulbous root. These western survey kāṇḍ-/kand- and devoiced kānt- forms fit that bulb/onion family; source nasal/retroflex spellings are preserved. They are separated from the granthi knot-derived gaṇḍ-/gaṇṭh- onion words.

Turner’s granthi knot family explicitly includes Sindhi gaṇḍhi onion bulb and Lahnda gaḍḍh onion/gaṇḍhā bulb, beside Hindi gā̃ṭhī/gā̃ṭhā. The Gujari/Dogri and Haryanvi/Buksa onion responses match this documented bulb sense; nasal versus written nasal-stop and aspiration realizations remain as transcribed. The unrelated kanda onion series is kept separate.
